{"evidence": [{"id": "E620d3ddaad5ad2054c752d19", "chunk_id": "779175155be2b4c482fd5c25", "parent_id": "a246f31f42c4cc1a08a38919", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L79-L98", "content": "To improve privacy in shared environments, vLLM supports isolating prefix cache reuse through optional per-request salting.
By including a `cache_salt` in the request, this value is injected into the hash of the first block, ensuring that only requests with the same salt can reuse cached KV blocks.
This prevents timing-based attacks where an adversary could infer cached content by observing latency differences.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E881a6028445aaeece4403f8c", "chunk_id": "a756e1212e535b1d75e47a3f", "parent_id": "5e18fdc07bd0b1d756518f71", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L178-L192", "content": "In v0, when detecting block 3 is duplicated, we free block 3 and let Request 2 use block 1 instead, so its block table becomes `[0, 1]` in Time 1.
However, the block table in vLLM v1 is append-only, meaning that changing the block table from `[0, 3]` to `[0, 1]` is not allowed.
As a result, we will have duplicated blocks for the hash key E-H.
This duplication will be eliminated when the request is freed.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E5cd53a2e3cb929c22be31ed5", "chunk_id": "a3e5c4e7c85d6b5597e79aa6", "parent_id": "2cea061deb042236c244b028", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L15-L19", "content": "* Parent hash value: The hash value of the parent hash block.
* Block tokens: A tuple of tokens in this block.
The reason to include the exact tokens is to reduce potential hash value collision.
* Extra hashes: Other values required to make this block unique, such as LoRA IDs, multi-modality input hashes (see the example below), and cache salts to isolate caches in multi-tenant environments.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "Ea15ac575d0077997740e8e1e", "chunk_id": "831e35484dd2ca27088ebde3", "parent_id": "49360f163824e6436d30ab06", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L24-L29", "content": "!!
! note "Note 2"
The above hash key structure is not 100% collision free.
Theoretically it’s still possible for the different prefix tokens to have the same hash value.
To avoid any hash collisions **in a multi-tenant setup, we advise to use SHA256** as hash function instead of the default builtin hash.
SHA256 is supported since vLLM v0.8.3 and must be enabled with a command line argument.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E1c5b7341c4d64d891d9a1cfe", "chunk_id": "7c1a6df7e7a23c7671ff1794", "parent_id": "a246f31f42c4cc1a08a38919", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L79-L98", "content": "!!
! note
Cache isolation is not supported in engine V0.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E18df8d7de69a9bc239731abf", "chunk_id": "28bc81fe7e8f333b5d5c57d9", "parent_id": "a246f31f42c4cc1a08a38919", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L79-L98", "content": "In the rest of this document, we first introduce the data structure used for prefix caching in vLLM v1, followed by the prefix caching workflow of major KV cache operators (e.g., allocate, append, free, eviction).
Finally, we use an example to illustrate the end to end prefix caching workflow.
**Cache Isolation for Security**", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E0362c6dc8d47bfd883c8dba8", "chunk_id": "410eaf3456d68525428df1d4", "parent_id": "a246f31f42c4cc1a08a38919", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L79-L98", "content": "This offers protection without compromising performance.
```json
{
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Here is a document with details about the world series: ..."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Who won the world series in 2020?"}
  ],
  "cache_salt": "your-cache-salt"
}
```", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E2e11ed500d592310a7422ca6", "chunk_id": "06a4698c9e4cb362ac120a20", "parent_id": "a246f31f42c4cc1a08a38919", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L79-L98", "content": "With this setup, cache sharing is limited to users or requests that explicitly agree on a common salt, enabling cache reuse within a trust group while isolating others.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "Eb84bdda9ff6e6568d86f5bd3", "chunk_id": "95411643ef936e459d8993e9", "parent_id": "2cea061deb042236c244b028", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L15-L19", "content": "In the example above, the KV cache in the first block can be uniquely identified with the token “A gentle breeze stirred”.

{"task": "vLLM cache_salt 加到哪个 block 的 hash？跨租户复用有什么条件，V0支持吗？", "evidence": [{"id": "E620d3ddaad5ad2054c752d19", "chunk_id": "779175155be2b4c482fd5c25", "parent_id": "a246f31f42c4cc1a08a38919", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L79-L98", "content": "To improve privacy in shared environments, vLLM supports isolating prefix cache reuse through optional per-request salting.
By including a `cache_salt` in the request, this value is injected into the hash of the first block, ensuring that only requests with the same salt can reuse cached KV blocks.
This prevents timing-based attacks where an adversary could infer cached content by observing latency differences.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E881a6028445aaeece4403f8c", "chunk_id": "a756e1212e535b1d75e47a3f", "parent_id": "5e18fdc07bd0b1d756518f71", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L178-L192", "content": "In v0, when detecting block 3 is duplicated, we free block 3 and let Request 2 use block 1 instead, so its block table becomes `[0, 1]` in Time 1.
However, the block table in vLLM v1 is append-only, meaning that changing the block table from `[0, 3]` to `[0, 1]` is not allowed.
As a result, we will have duplicated blocks for the hash key E-H.
This duplication will be eliminated when the request is freed.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E5cd53a2e3cb929c22be31ed5", "chunk_id": "a3e5c4e7c85d6b5597e79aa6", "parent_id": "2cea061deb042236c244b028", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L15-L19", "content": "* Parent hash value: The hash value of the parent hash block.
* Block tokens: A tuple of tokens in this block.
The reason to include the exact tokens is to reduce potential hash value collision.
* Extra hashes: Other values required to make this block unique, such as LoRA IDs, multi-modality input hashes (see the example below), and cache salts to isolate caches in multi-tenant environments.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "Ea15ac575d0077997740e8e1e", "chunk_id": "831e35484dd2ca27088ebde3", "parent_id": "49360f163824e6436d30ab06", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L24-L29", "content": "!!
! note "Note 2"
The above hash key structure is not 100% collision free.
Theoretically it’s still possible for the different prefix tokens to have the same hash value.
To avoid any hash collisions **in a multi-tenant setup, we advise to use SHA256** as hash function instead of the default builtin hash.
SHA256 is supported since vLLM v0.8.3 and must be enabled with a command line argument.", "truncated": false, "metadata": {"release": "v0.10.2", "commit": "01efc7ef781391e744ed08c3292817a773d654e6", "source_type": "documentation"}}, {"id": "E1c5b7341c4d64d891d9a1cfe", "chunk_id": "7c1a6df7e7a23c7671ff1794", "parent_id": "a246f31f42c4cc1a08a38919", "source": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md", "sha256": "0a8a9e9095055c4f8e0cdaf078e3194ab06428222d65abb9c827f6879607ce61", "locator": "/Users/jennyma/Projects/InfraAgent/evals/agent-e2e-v1/corpus/vllm-prefix_caching.md#L79-L98", "content": "!!

delivered.content:
To improve privacy in shared environments, vLLM supports isolating prefix cache reuse through optional per-request salting.
By including a `cache_salt` in the request, this value is injected into the hash of the first block, ensuring that only requests with the same salt can reuse cached KV blocks.
This prevents timing-based attacks where an adversary could infer cached content by observing latency differences.

In v0, when detecting block 3 is duplicated, we free block 3 and let Request 2 use block 1 instead, so its block table becomes `[0, 1]` in Time 1.
However, the block table in vLLM v1 is append-only, meaning that changing the block table from `[0, 3]` to `[0, 1]` is not allowed.
As a result, we will have duplicated blocks for the hash key E-H.
This duplication will be eliminated when the request is freed.

* Parent hash value: The hash value of the parent hash block.
* Block tokens: A tuple of tokens in this block.
The reason to include the exact tokens is to reduce potential hash value collision.
* Extra hashes: Other values required to make this block unique, such as LoRA IDs, multi-modality input hashes (see the example below), and cache salts to isolate caches in multi-tenant environments.

!!
! note "Note 2"
The above hash key structure is not 100% collision free.
Theoretically it’s still possible for the different prefix tokens to have the same hash value.
To avoid any hash collisions **in a multi-tenant setup, we advise to use SHA256** as hash function instead of the default builtin hash.
SHA256 is supported since vLLM v0.8.3 and must be enabled with a command line argument.

!!
! note
Cache isolation is not supported in engine V0.

In the rest of this document, we first introduce the data structure used for prefix caching in vLLM v1, followed by the prefix caching workflow of major KV cache operators (e.g., allocate, append, free, eviction).
Finally, we use an example to illustrate the end to end prefix caching workflow.
**Cache Isolation for Security**
With this setup, cache sharing is limited to users or requests that explicitly agree on a common salt, enabling cache reuse within a trust group while isolating others.

In the rest of this document, we first introduce the data structure used for prefix caching in vLLM v1, followed by the prefix caching workflow of major KV cache operators (e.g., allocate, append, free, eviction).
Finally, we use an example to illustrate the end to end prefix caching workflow.
**Cache Isolation for Security**
With this setup, cache sharing is limited to users or requests that explicitly agree on a common salt, enabling cache reuse within a trust group while isolating others.

In the example above, the KV cache in the first block can be uniquely identified with the token “A gentle breeze stirred”.
The third block can be uniquely identified with the tokens in the block “laughed in the distance”, along with the prefix tokens “A gentle breeze stirred the leaves as children”.
